Head-and-shoulders portrait bust of one soldier, three-quarter view, the face turned toward the right side of the image. Square image. Framing: the top of the head or headgear about 9% from the top edge, the eyes about 39% from the top, the chin about 62% from the top, the image cut at mid-chest, with dark empty space above and around the head. One figure only. This card must never look like the Longbow Hunter's: the militiaman is not hooded and not an archer. Lighting: a single warm candle key light from the upper left, a dim warm fill, deep warm shadows, and a thin soft warm rim light along the back of the head or headgear, the hair and the shoulders that separates the whole silhouette clearly from the background. Background: plain, unpatterned, very dark warm brown close to #1C1A17, with no objects.
Medium: painterly oil on a wood panel, visible brushwork, moderate detail, a strong readable silhouette: the shape of the headgear and the light face against the dark background must still read when the image is shrunk to 48 pixels.
Colors: muted and earthy, except the side's deep bottle-green cloth (#1F6A50), the green of jade in shade, which shows clearly on the hood folded down on his shoulders and on the tabard over his chest, as on the figure, so the card reads as that side at a glance. Nothing in the image glows.

Subject: A fighter of the Thornwood, forest clans who live among ancient trees: weathered bark-brown skin, bark-and-leaf clothing and armor in moss green and bark brown.
A Thorn Militia levy spearman: a bark-brown leather jerkin, worn under a sleeveless tabard of deep bottle-green cloth that covers his whole chest and belly from the collar down to just below the knees, front and back, split at the front below the belt so the legs can stride and held at the waist by a knotted rope belt; a short deep bottle-green hooded cloak, the hood pushed back and lying in folds on the shoulders; padded sleeves and leather bracers; wrapped legs and soft boots; bark-brown weathered skin; a long dark hawthorn spear with a barbed head of bone and iron shaped like a great thorn. No shield, no antlers. Plain and poor.
Person: a poor levy spearman, not a leader; an ordinary weathered, open face of the nation under a small cap of hardened bark; not hooded, not an archer, no bow and no quiver.
